summary:
ORBITFORGE, developed by two passionate 18 year olds, is an interactive, NASA-inspired space mission app designed to make spacecraft engineering and space exploration accessible, engaging, and educational.

Developed using Visual Studio Code, Python, and the Godot game engine, we developed a platform where users can design their own spacecraft, manage financial and technical constraints, and navigate through a 3D space environment. Our project integrates real scientific information from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) asteroid database, connecting interactive gameplay with authentic space research.

Inspired by NASA's CubeSat 101 guidelines, we incorporated an engineering laboratory that evaluates spacecraft mass, power consumption, and mission readiness. In addition, one of our majors is cybersecurity, which inspired us to develop a simulation to demonstrate how digital threats can affect spacecraft systems.

ORBITFORGE addresses the challenge by transforming complex space mission concepts into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. Instead of just simply reading about space exploration, users can actively experiment with spacecraft design, engineering trade-offs, and mission planning.

Our project aims to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers by bridging the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application.
details:
ORBITFORGE — ACG Asteri

Design. Defend. Discover.

ORBITFORGE is an interactive, NASA-inspired spacecraft engineering and space mission design game developed by ACG Asteri for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project transforms the complexities of space mission design into an accessible, immersive, and educational experience, enabling users to think and make decisions like real mission engineers.

How Our Project Works

ORBITFORGE guides players through an interconnected spacecraft development and exploration experience. Users begin by designing their spacecraft, selecting essential components such as propulsion systems and solar panels while considering and managing financial and engineering constraints. Each decision introduces trade-offs involving spacecraft mass, electrical power, fuel consumption, and mission readiness.

Inspired by NASA's CubeSat 101 guidelines, our integrated engineering laboratory encourages players to evaluate their spacecraft's technical feasibility before launch.

A distinguishing and rather highly creative feature of ORBITFORGE is its integration of real astronomical reference data from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) Small-Body Database. Players can retrieve scientific information about asteroid 433 Eros, including its orbital classification, orbital period, and near-Earth-object status. By incorporating authentic astronomical information into a simulated mission environment, we bridge the gap between real-world space research and interactive gameplay.

Following spacecraft construction, players can launch into a three-dimensional space environment, navigate toward a simulated celestial target, monitor fuel and battery consumption, conduct scientific observations, and receive performance scores based on mission outcomes.

ORBITFORGE also incorporates an educational cybersecurity component, allowing players to investigate fictional spacecraft security threats, recognize suspicious commands, and explore defensive responses. This emphasizes that successful space exploration depends not only on physical engineering but also on the reliability and security of digital systems.

Technologies and Development

Our team developed ORBITFORGE using several complementary technologies:

  • Godot 4 and GDScript: For 3D spacecraft modelling, interactive gameplay, mission navigation, and user interfaces.
  • Python and FastAPI: For backend functionality, mission processing, engineering analysis, and application programming interfaces.
  • SQLite: For storing mission configurations, results, and audit information.
  • Visual Studio Code: For programming, debugging, and organizing our development workflow.
  • NASA JPL APIs: For accessing authentic astronomical reference information.

The project also incorporates simulated telemetry, mission analytics, risk evaluation, and engineering optimization concepts to demonstrate how mission planners assess competing technical requirements.

Creativity and Innovation

ORBITFORGE's innovation lies in combining spacecraft construction, scientific data exploration, engineering decision-making, cybersecurity education, and 3D gameplay within a single learning environment.

Rather than presenting space engineering as a collection of disconnected theoretical concepts, our project allows users to experience the relationships between engineering choices and mission outcomes. For example, installing additional spacecraft components may improve functionality while increasing mass, costs, or power requirements.

Our integration of cybersecurity introduces another dimension often overlooked in introductory space education: the importance of protecting spacecraft commands, telemetry, and mission-critical systems.

By transforming technical constraints into interactive challenges, ORBITFORGE encourages curiosity, critical thinking, experimentation, and interdisciplinary problem-solving.

Design Considerations and Challenges

Throughout development, ACG Asteri prioritized educational accessibility, technical feasibility, scientific relevance, and responsible simulation design.

We considered how to simplify complex aerospace concepts without misrepresenting the underlying science. Consequently, spacecraft performance calculations, flight dynamics, cybersecurity incidents, and engineering limits are presented as educational simulations.

We also considered the accessibility of our platform, designing an experience that allows users without advanced programming or aerospace engineering knowledge to engage with mission design concepts to successfully design and launch their own spacecraft!

Integrating different development environments, connecting a Python backend with Godot, incorporating external scientific data, and balancing interactive gameplay with meaningful engineering principles were central challenges that shaped our approach.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ORBITFORGE aims to make space science and engineering more open source to all, engaging, and inclusive, particularly for students and aspiring scientists.

Through interactive learning, users can develop a stronger understanding of spacecraft subsystems, mission planning, resource management, scientific observation, and cybersecurity (cyberattacks are increasingly globally, our team immediately thought of incorporating this into our game)

Our long-term vision is to expand ORBITFORGE into a broader educational platform featuring additional celestial destinations, more sophisticated spacecraft systems, and improving realistic mission scenarios.

Ultimately, ORBITFORGE seeks to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, programmers, and space explorers by demonstrating that space mission design is not merely based on heavy theory in physics class, but it is indeed something to explore, experiment with, and experience.

ACG Asteri believes that the future of space exploration begins with curiosity and education, ORBITFORGE successfully transforms this into an interactive mission.
